dataset_title: Foundation Medicine Adult Cancer Clinical Dataset (FM-AD)
question: What are the mutation frequencies and co-occurrence patterns of clinically targeted genes in a large real-world oncology population?
rationale: 18,004 patients profiled on a clinical panel give tight confidence intervals on alteration frequencies, including for alterations too rare to study in a thousand-patient research cohort. Frequency and co-occurrence need only the variant calls and the tumor type, both of which are present.

dataset_title: Foundation Medicine Adult Cancer Clinical Dataset (FM-AD)
question: How does the mutational landscape of clinically sequenced patients differ from that of research cohorts such as TCGA?
rationale: Clinical sequencing populations are enriched for advanced and pretreated disease relative to the largely treatment-naive primary tumors in research cohorts. With 18,004 cases the comparison is well powered, and the discrepancy is itself a caution about generalising research-cohort findings to clinical practice.

dataset_title: Foundation Medicine Adult Cancer Clinical Dataset (FM-AD)
question: How common are actionable alterations across tumor types in routine practice?
rationale: Scale plus a clinically-deployed panel makes this the right cohort for estimating what fraction of patients would be eligible for a given targeted therapy, a question that research cohorts systematically answer wrong.

dataset_title: Acute Myeloid Leukemia
question: How does the genomic landscape of paediatric AML differ from adult AML?
rationale: 2,281 RNA-sequenced paediatric cases can be contrasted directly with adult AML cohorts, and the marker paper established that the differences are substantial and age-dependent. This remains the definitive paediatric comparison set.

dataset_title: Acute Myeloid Leukemia
question: Which molecular features predict survival in paediatric AML?
rationale: Vital status informative for 86.6% of 2,492 cases with median follow-up of 41.7 months gives a well-powered survival cohort, and therapeutic agents are recorded for 35% so treatment can be partially controlled.

dataset_title: Acute Myeloid Leukemia
question: Are there racial differences in paediatric AML biology or outcome?
rationale: 251 Black or African American patients alongside 1,551 white patients is one of the better-powered settings in this corpus for a race-stratified comparison in a paediatric cancer.

dataset_title: CPTAC-Brain, Head and Neck, Kidney, Lung, Pancreas, Uterus
question: Which genomic alterations have consequences at the protein level, and which do not?
rationale: This is the question CPTAC exists to answer, and it needs both halves joined. Genomics on over 1,800 cases here pairs with proteomic studies in the PDC on the same participants, allowing copy number and mutation effects to be traced to protein and phosphosite abundance.

dataset_title: CPTAC-Brain, Head and Neck, Kidney, Lung, Pancreas, Uterus
question: What molecular features predict recurrence across cancer types?
rationale: Progression or recurrence is informative for 77.9% of 1,866 cases with a median follow-up of 22.8 months - unusual completeness for a recurrence endpoint, and the basis for a genuinely pan-cancer recurrence analysis.

dataset_title: CPTAC-Brain, Head and Neck, Kidney, Lung, Pancreas, Uterus
question: Do proteogenomic subtypes cut across tissue of origin?
rationale: Six cancer types collected prospectively under a common protocol make cross-tissue subtype comparison less confounded by collection differences than a retrospective pan-cancer assembly.

dataset_title: Molecular Profiling to Predict Response to Treatment for Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
question: Which genomic features predict failure of protocolised induction therapy in paediatric B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia?
rationale: Treatment outcome and regimen are populated for 100% of 1,510 cases, and regimen strings name the actual protocol arm, so response can be modeled within a treatment context rather than across an uncontrolled mixture of therapies. Whole genome sequencing on 1,507 cases supports genome-wide discovery at this sample size.

dataset_title: Molecular Profiling to Predict Response to Treatment for Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
question: Do Hispanic or Latino children carry a different genomic landscape or a different response profile, and does genomics explain any of the known outcome disparity?
rationale: 333 of 1,510 patients are recorded as Hispanic or Latino - both a substantial absolute number and a substantial share, which is unusual. With treatment held closer to constant by the trial protocol, the ethnicity contrast is less confounded by care access than in an observational cohort.

dataset_title: Molecular Profiling to Predict Response to Treatment for Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
question: What are the long-term survival determinants in paediatric ALL, given follow-up that extends beyond fifteen years?
rationale: Vital status is informative for 84% of cases and median follow-up is 100.2 months, so late relapse and long-term survival are genuinely observable rather than censored away. Very few genomic cohorts of this size reach this follow-up duration.

dataset_title: Molecular Profiling to Predict Response to Treatment for Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
question: How do subtype-defining fusions and copy number alterations interact with assigned risk group and delivered therapy?
rationale: Structural variant and copy number calls exist for 1,504 cases, and the regimen field records the risk-stratified arm each patient received, allowing molecular subtype to be crossed with the therapy actually delivered.

dataset_title: Breast Invasive Carcinoma
question: Does a new computational method reproduce established breast cancer molecular subtypes?
rationale: Expression, methylation, copy number, microRNA and protein array data on largely the same 1,098 tumors, with subtype assignments established across hundreds of prior papers. This is the standard benchmark, and the density of prior work is the point.

dataset_title: Breast Invasive Carcinoma
question: Which molecular features are associated with response to specific systemic therapies?
rationale: Therapeutic agents are recorded for 71% of cases - cyclophosphamide, tamoxifen, anastrozole, paclitaxel and doxorubicin are the commonest - and a treatment outcome field is populated for 64%. Combined with expression on 1,095 cases this supports agent-stratified response analysis.

dataset_title: Breast Invasive Carcinoma
question: Do radiology or pathology image features add prognostic information beyond molecular data?
rationale: Imaging for these same patients is held in the Imaging Data Commons and is openly downloadable, while the molecular data sit in the GDC. Joining them gives a multimodal cohort most users never realise is available.

dataset_title: Breast Invasive Carcinoma
question: What distinguishes long-term survivors, given a median follow-up of 27.1 months?
rationale: Vital status is informative for 99.9% of cases and follow-up time is computable, giving a clean overall survival endpoint on a large cohort.

dataset_title: NCI Cancer Model Development for the Human Cancer Model Initiative
question: How faithfully do patient-derived models retain the genomics of their source tumor?
rationale: Models and their source tumors are both characterized, with near-complete whole genome coverage, which makes fidelity measurable rather than assumed. The answer determines how much any model-based result should be trusted.

dataset_title: NCI Cancer Model Development for the Human Cancer Model Initiative
question: Can a usable model system be found for a rare cancer that currently has none?
rationale: Coverage spans many tumor types including rare ones. For a researcher working on a cancer with no established cell line, this is often the only route to any model at all, and it is the cohort's most practically valuable use.

dataset_title: NCI Cancer Model Development for the Human Cancer Model Initiative
question: Does prior treatment of the donor shape the derived model's biology?
rationale: Prior treatment is informative for 88.9% of donors and treatment given is recorded for all, so models derived from treated and untreated patients can be compared - a question with direct bearing on how model-based drug screens should be interpreted.

dataset_title: Glioblastoma Multiforme
question: Do imaging features add prognostic or subtype information beyond molecular data in glioblastoma?
rationale: Radiology on 607 cases and pathology slides on 389, paired with expression on 293, methylation on 423 and copy number on 599 for the same patients. Glioma is the disease where imaging is most clinically central, and this pairing is openly available.

dataset_title: Glioblastoma Multiforme
question: Does a new glioma classifier reproduce established methylation subgroups?
rationale: Methylation on 423 cases with subgroup definitions established across a large literature makes this the standard validation set for glioma classification.

dataset_title: Glioblastoma Multiforme
question: Which molecular features associate with survival in glioblastoma?
rationale: Vital status is informative for 96.3% of 617 cases, giving a clean overall survival endpoint on a well-characterized cohort.

dataset_title: Comprehensive genomic characterization of radiation-related papillary thyroid cancer in the Ukraine
question: What is the mutational and structural signature of ionising radiation exposure in a solid human tumor, and how does it scale with dose?
rationale: Whole genome sequencing on 395 cases with structural variant and copy number calls on 394 supports genome-wide signature analysis, including the fusion-driven and small-deletion patterns the marker paper associated with radiation. This is the cohort's central strength and the reason it was assembled.

dataset_title: Comprehensive genomic characterization of radiation-related papillary thyroid cancer in the Ukraine
question: Do radiation-associated papillary thyroid carcinomas differ transcriptionally from sporadic ones, and can a classifier separate them?
rationale: RNA sequencing on 438 cases and microRNA on 437 gives a well-powered expression cohort. TCGA-THCA provides a 507-case sporadic comparison group in the same repository with the same harmonization, which makes a cross-cohort contrast unusually tractable.

dataset_title: Comprehensive genomic characterization of radiation-related papillary thyroid cancer in the Ukraine
question: Does age at exposure shape the resulting tumor genome, given that participants were children or in utero at the time?
rationale: The cohort's defining feature is exposure during a developmental window. Age variables together with the genomic data allow the question to be posed, and it is one of the few human settings where exposure timing is externally fixed by a single dated event rather than self-reported.

dataset_title: Comprehensive genomic characterization of radiation-related papillary thyroid cancer in the Ukraine
question: Can microRNA profiles discriminate radiation-associated thyroid tumors, as a cheaper assay than whole genome sequencing for future screening cohorts?
rationale: microRNA data exist on 437 of 449 cases, an unusually complete layer, and microRNA assays are far more tractable in resource-limited screening settings than sequencing.

dataset_title: HIV+ Tumor Molecular Characterization Project - Cervical Cancer
question: Does HPV clade shape the tumor epigenome and transcriptome differently in an African cohort than in the predominantly North American and European cohorts that define current cervical cancer subtypes?
rationale: Methylation arrays are available on 120 cases and RNA sequencing on 123, on the same tumors as whole genome sequencing that can be used to type and subclassify the integrated HPV. This is the design the marker paper used, and the cohort is large enough to repeat it with different clade groupings or to test subtype assignments derived from TCGA-CESC against an independent, differently constituted population.

dataset_title: HIV+ Tumor Molecular Characterization Project - Cervical Cancer
question: Do molecular subtypes derived from predominantly white cohorts transfer to Black African patients, or do they misclassify tumors in this population?
rationale: 207 of 212 cases are recorded as Black or African American, making this the only cohort in this corpus where a non-white group constitutes more than half the participants. Expression and methylation data allow subtype classifiers trained on TCGA to be applied directly, and classifier failure is itself the finding.

dataset_title: HIV+ Tumor Molecular Characterization Project - Cervical Cancer
question: Which molecular features are associated with performance status and with response to chemoradiation in a setting where platinum-based chemoradiation is the dominant treatment?
rationale: ECOG performance status is informative on 98.6% of cases, which is exceptional - most GDC projects record it for none. Treatment type is populated for every case, therapeutic agents for 29.7% (cisplatin, paclitaxel and carboplatin are the commonest), and a treatment outcome field is populated for 67.9%. Together these support a response analysis that is impossible in most cohorts of this size.

dataset_title: HIV+ Tumor Molecular Characterization Project - Cervical Cancer
question: How do survival patterns in this cohort compare with cervical cancer cohorts from high-income settings, given a median follow-up of only 13.2 months?
rationale: Vital status is informative for 100% of cases and follow-up time is computable, giving a usable overall survival endpoint. The short follow-up is itself scientifically interesting because it reflects real-world attrition in the setting where the cohort was recruited.

dataset_title: HIV+ Tumor Molecular Characterization Project - Cervical Cancer
question: Can radiology and histopathology images from this cohort be used to build or validate imaging models on a population that is absent from almost every public imaging training set?
rationale: Histopathology and radiology are both available for 211 of 212 cases, alongside the molecular data. Imaging models trained largely on North American and European cohorts have documented performance gaps on under-represented populations, and this is one of the few resources that permits an external check.

dataset_title: NSCLC Radiogenomics
question: Do quantitative CT or PET features predict gene expression programs in lung adenocarcinoma?
rationale: This is the defining radiogenomics question and it needs paired data on the same patients, which this collection provides for the subset with matched microarrays. Imaging is available for all 211.

dataset_title: NSCLC Radiogenomics
question: How reproducible are radiomic features across CT and PET acquisitions of the same tumor?
rationale: Both modalities were acquired for the same patients pre-surgically, so feature stability across modality and acquisition can be assessed directly - a prerequisite for any radiomics claim and rarely testable.

dataset_title: NSCLC Radiogenomics
question: Can models trained on this cohort's segmentations generalize to other lung imaging collections in the same repository?
rationale: Expert segmentations and semantic annotations are provided, and the Imaging Data Commons holds several other lung collections that can serve as external validation within one access framework.

dataset_title: CPTAC STAD Study
question: How do distinct post-translational modification layers diverge from each other and from transcript abundance on the same tumors?
rationale: Phosphorylation, acetylation, glycosylation and ubiquitylation are measured on largely the same 184 to 193 tumors. Comparing regulation across four modification types on one cohort is an analysis this dataset uniquely enables; almost every other resource offers at most two.

dataset_title: CPTAC STAD Study
question: Does protein degradation signaling, read from the ubiquitylome, identify tumor subgroups invisible to transcriptomics?
rationale: Ubiquitylome data on 184 cases is among the largest such datasets anywhere. Degradation is a major regulatory axis that expression data cannot see, and a cohort this size makes subgroup discovery feasible rather than anecdotal.

dataset_title: CPTAC STAD Study
question: How does tumor metabolism, measured directly rather than inferred, relate to signaling state?
rationale: Metabolomics on 187 cases is available alongside the phosphoproteome, so metabolic state can be related to signaling directly instead of being inferred from enzyme transcript levels - which is what most metabolic analyses in cancer actually do.

dataset_title: CPTAC STAD Study
question: Can measured protein-protein interaction data improve network inference over correlation-based approaches?
rationale: Interaction data on 153 cases is exceptionally rare in a tumor cohort, and provides a measured reference against which inferred co-expression networks can be scored.

dataset_title: CPTAC AML Study
question: How does lipid composition differ across AML subtypes, and does it relate to differentiation state?
rationale: Lipidomic profiles on 98 primary AML samples, alongside proteome on all 164, allow lipid class abundance to be related to protein markers of myeloid differentiation on the same patients. Measured lipidomics on primary AML at this scale is essentially unavailable elsewhere.

dataset_title: CPTAC AML Study
question: Do measured metabolite levels agree with metabolic state inferred from transcript or protein abundance?
rationale: Metabolomics and proteomics on the same 98 patients allow a direct test of an assumption that a large body of computational metabolic modeling depends on and rarely gets to check.

dataset_title: CPTAC AML Study
question: Does protein acetylation, a modification tightly coupled to metabolic cofactor availability, track measured metabolite levels?
rationale: Acetylome on 164 cases and metabolome on 98 overlap substantially. Acetylation depends on acetyl-CoA availability, so this cohort can test a mechanistic link that is usually assumed rather than measured.

dataset_title: CPTAC AML Study
question: Can glycoproteomic features stratify AML in ways expression cannot?
rationale: Glycoproteome on all 164 cases; cell-surface glycosylation is directly relevant to immunotherapy target selection in myeloid disease.

dataset_title: The Cellular Geography of Therapeutic Resistance in Cancer
question: Where within a tumor do cells that survive therapy actually reside?
rationale: Multiplexed tissue imaging with single-cell RNA sequencing on the same specimens, in an atlas designed around this question, with therapy records available as a clinical component to define the treatment context.

dataset_title: The Cellular Geography of Therapeutic Resistance in Cancer
question: Do spatial niches associated with resistance recur across cancer types, or are they tissue-specific?
rationale: Neighborhood definitions derived here can be tested against other HTAN atlases that share the multiplexed imaging component, giving cross-atlas comparison within a single access framework and a common data model.

dataset_title: The Cellular Geography of Therapeutic Resistance in Cancer
question: Can the extended clinical tier be used to relate spatial organization to real treatment sequences rather than to treatment as a single binary?
rationale: This atlas carries the extended clinical data tier that most atlases lack, alongside therapy and follow-up. That is what allows spatial features to be related to what was actually given and what happened next.

dataset_title: CPTAC LUAD Discovery Study
question: Which proteins are regulated by degradation rather than by transcription in lung adenocarcinoma?
rationale: Ubiquitylome on 80 cases alongside proteome on all 115 allows the two regulatory modes to be separated on the same tumors - the direct test of an assumption that expression studies make implicitly.

dataset_title: CPTAC LUAD Discovery Study
question: How do acetylation and phosphorylation interact in the same tumor?
rationale: Both modification layers are measured on all 115 cases, allowing cross-modification analysis on a common set of tumors rather than across separate cohorts.

dataset_title: CPTAC LUAD Discovery Study
question: Can degradation signatures identify candidate targets for proteasome or E3 ligase directed therapy?
rationale: Direct measurement of ubiquitylation state in primary tumors is the substrate for target nomination in a therapeutic area where target selection is usually based on inference.

dataset_title: Genomic Characterization of Metastatic Castration Resistant Prostate Cancer
question: What distinguishes the genome of metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer from primary prostate cancer?
rationale: Whole genome sequencing on all 101 metastatic biopsies pairs naturally with TCGA-PRAD's 500 primary tumors in the same repository under the same harmonization. The contrast is the cohort's clearest use and does not depend on any outcome field.

dataset_title: Genomic Characterization of Metastatic Castration Resistant Prostate Cancer
question: Which transcriptional programs mark androgen receptor pathway independence and neuroendocrine transdifferentiation in treatment-resistant disease?
rationale: RNA sequencing on 99 metastatic biopsies is the right substrate for AR-signaling and neuroendocrine scoring, and metastatic tissue is where these phenotypes actually occur.

dataset_title: Genomic Characterization of Metastatic Castration Resistant Prostate Cancer
question: How do structural variants and genome rearrangement patterns differ between metastatic sites?
rationale: Structural variant calls exist for all 101 cases from whole genome rather than exome data, which is what makes rearrangement analysis credible here.

dataset_title: Genomic Characterization of Metastatic Castration Resistant Prostate Cancer
question: Can expression or genomic features predict which metastatic biopsies come from patients with the most aggressive disease trajectory?
rationale: This is the question most people want the cohort for, and it is the one the harmonized records cannot support. It is listed here to be explicit that it requires outcome data obtained separately.

dataset_title: Pancreas Cancer Organoid Profiling
question: Which molecular features predict chemotherapy sensitivity in pancreatic cancer organoids?
rationale: Exome on 69 and expression on 49 organoids, with measured drug responses reported in the source publication. Because response is measured experimentally rather than inferred from clinical records, this avoids the treatment confounding that defeats observational response analysis.

dataset_title: Pancreas Cancer Organoid Profiling
question: How faithfully do organoids recapitulate the genomics of the tumors they came from?
rationale: A model-fidelity question that determines how much weight any organoid result deserves, and one that can be posed here because both the organoid profiles and the source tumor stage information are available.

dataset_title: Pancreas Cancer Organoid Profiling
question: Can organoid expression programs stratify pancreatic cancer subtypes established in tissue cohorts?
rationale: Expression on 49 organoids can be scored against the basal-like and classical subtype definitions derived from bulk tumor cohorts, testing whether those subtypes survive in culture.

dataset_title: HIV+ Tumor Molecular Characterization Project - Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
question: How does the genomic landscape of HIV-associated diffuse large B-cell lymphoma differ from that of lymphoma in immunocompetent patients?
rationale: Whole genome sequencing on 66 cases from an HIV-enriched population, contrastable with the many DLBCL cohorts derived from largely HIV-negative populations. Whole genome rather than exome makes structural and viral-integration analysis possible.

dataset_title: HIV+ Tumor Molecular Characterization Project - Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
question: Does immune status shape the tumor transcriptome in lymphoma?
rationale: RNA sequencing on 55 cases with ECOG performance status on 71% allows transcriptional programs to be related to a clinical proxy for host status.

dataset_title: HIV+ Tumor Molecular Characterization Project - Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
question: What are the outcomes of HIV-associated DLBCL treated with standard regimens?
rationale: Vital status is informative for 76% of cases, follow-up is derivable for 57 of 70 with a median of 11.3 months extending to 99.6, and 24% carry a named regimen.

dataset_title: CTSP Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL) CALGB 50303
question: Do molecular subtypes of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma predict differential benefit from dose-adjusted EPOCH-R versus R-CHOP?
rationale: This is a predictive-biomarker question, and it requires randomized treatment assignment to answer properly. RNA sequencing on 44 cases supports cell-of-origin and subtype classification, and the trial provides the randomization.

dataset_title: CTSP Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL) CALGB 50303
question: How well do molecular classifiers built on observational DLBCL cohorts perform on uniformly treated trial patients?
rationale: Classifier performance usually degrades when treatment heterogeneity is removed, because some apparent prognostic signal is really treatment-selection signal. A uniformly treated, randomized cohort is the right place to detect that.

dataset_title: CTSP Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL) CALGB 50303
question: What is the five-year survival experience of genomically characterized DLBCL patients treated in a controlled setting?
rationale: Vital status is informative for all 45 cases with 60.4 months of median follow-up and cause of death recorded for 35.6% - unusually complete for a cohort this small.

dataset_title: HIV+ Tumor Molecular Characterization Project - Lung Cancer
question: Does lung cancer arising in people living with HIV differ genomically from lung cancer in the general population?
rationale: Whole genome sequencing on all 39 cases, contrastable with the large TCGA lung cohorts in the same repository under the same harmonization. Whole genome rather than exome allows mutational signature and structural analysis.

dataset_title: HIV+ Tumor Molecular Characterization Project - Lung Cancer
question: Can this cohort serve as a validation set for HIV-associated cancer hypotheses?
rationale: Alongside the cervical and lymphoma cohorts in the same program, it allows a hypothesis about HIV-associated tumor biology to be tested across three tumor types collected under a common protocol.

dataset_title: HIV+ Tumor Molecular Characterization Project - Lung Cancer
question: What is the survival experience of this population?
rationale: Vital status is informative for 89.7% of cases, with follow-up derivable for 36 of 39 and extending to 104 months despite a short median of 6.4.

dataset_title: Omic and Multidimensional Spatial Atlas of Metastatic Breast Cancers
question: How does the spatial organization of a metastatic tumor change as it acquires resistance to therapy?
rationale: Serial biopsies with multiplexed imaging and spatial transcriptomics on the same patients across treatment, with therapy and follow-up clinical components present. This longitudinal spatial design is essentially unique in public data.

dataset_title: Omic and Multidimensional Spatial Atlas of Metastatic Breast Cancers
question: Do single-cell chromatin accessibility changes precede the transcriptional changes that accompany resistance?
rationale: Single-cell ATAC and single-cell RNA on the same serial samples allow regulatory and transcriptional state to be ordered in time within a patient.

dataset_title: Omic and Multidimensional Spatial Atlas of Metastatic Breast Cancers
question: Can ultrastructural features from electron microscopy be related to molecular state measured on the same tissue?
rationale: Electron microscopy appears in no other dataset in this corpus. Linking ultrastructure to spatial and single-cell molecular data on the same specimens is possible only here.

dataset_title: Omic and Multidimensional Spatial Atlas of Metastatic Breast Cancers
question: How do multiplexed imaging and spatial transcriptomics agree when applied to the same tissue section?
rationale: Both assays are present on shared specimens, which makes cross-platform concordance measurable - a methodological question the spatial field needs answered and rarely can.
